accepted_units.context_note: The source constructs the Verdier quotient of a triangulated category by localizing at morphisms whose cones lie in a chosen triangulated subcategory. The quotient annihilates that subcategory and is characterized by unique factorization of exact functors that annihilate it; compatible adjoint functors descend, and full faithfulness can survive descent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires a triangulated category, a full triangulated subcategory, and the localization calculus asserted by the source. The universal property characterizes the quotient categorically; it does not select a concrete presentation of its objects or morphisms.
accepted_units.title: Define structural loss by a universal quotient
accepted_units.why_material: This is a reusable move for making deliberate information loss precise: specify what must become zero, invert exactly the morphisms witnessing that loss, and use the factorization property to test whether constructions descend canonically.

accepted_units.context_note: Admissibility is expressed through adjoints to a subcategory embedding and equivalently through exact triangles separating each object into a subcategory component and an orthogonal component. When admissibility holds, the quotient by the subcategory is equivalent to the appropriate orthogonal, and iterating the construction yields semiorthogonal decompositions; exceptional objects give especially simple pieces.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The replacement of a quotient by an orthogonal complement depends on existence and sidedness of adjoints. Semiorthogonal decompositions are ordered and need not be symmetric or canonical, and exceptional pieces exist only under additional hypotheses.
accepted_units.title: Replace an abstract quotient by an admissible orthogonal complement
accepted_units.why_material: It turns an opaque quotient into a constructive decomposition: identify a removable component, prove the required adjoint, and read the retained information in an orthogonal subcategory.

accepted_units.context_note: The graded and ungraded singularity categories are defined by quotienting bounded derived module categories by perfect complexes. Finite homological dimension makes the quotient trivial. Derived tensor constructions induce functors on singularity categories precisely when they send perfect complexes to perfect complexes, with adjoints available under stronger finiteness assumptions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses Noetherian module categories and the derived/perfect-complex presentation. Functoriality requires finite Tor-amplitude and perfectness over the target, and the stated right adjoint additionally needs finite generation over the source.
accepted_units.title: Isolate the nonperfect remainder and require maps to preserve what is discarded
accepted_units.why_material: This gives a generic semantic pattern: define the feature of interest as what remains after structurally resolvable objects are removed, then make preservation of the discarded class the exact descent condition for transformations.

accepted_units.context_note: Objects of a singularity quotient can, after a sufficiently large shift, be represented by modules with higher Ext vanishing. Under that condition, morphisms in the quotient are ordinary module maps modulo the subspace of maps that factor through projective modules.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The concrete morphism description requires the stated Ext-vanishing representative, obtained using sufficiently high truncations and finite injective dimension. Without those hypotheses the simple quotient formula need not apply directly.
accepted_units.title: Compute quotient morphisms by exposing the null factorizations
accepted_units.why_material: It replaces difficult roofs in a localization by a familiar map space with an explicit equivalence relation, showing how a representation choice and a vanishing condition can convert abstract quotient semantics into tractable data.

accepted_units.context_note: The quotient category of graded modules modulo finite-dimensional torsion is described through eventual tails: morphisms are a filtered limit over submodules with finite-dimensional quotient. Projection has a right adjoint, and under the source's finiteness conditions its derived restriction is fully faithful.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on connected Noetherian grading, the torsion notion induced by positive degree, condition chi for the restricted adjoint, and Gorenstein hypotheses for the bounded derived statement. Formula typography is fragmented in normalized text and should be checked before exact reuse.
accepted_units.title: Encode eventual behavior by quotienting finite prefixes
accepted_units.why_material: This is a reusable quotient move: declare finite initial data negligible, characterize the surviving morphisms through stable tails, and use an adjoint section to recover a controlled representative of the quotient object.

accepted_units.context_note: Two semiorthogonal decompositions of a common ambient derived category realize, respectively, the quotient-graded category and the singularity category as complementary components. Gorenstein duality aligns their orthogonals. The sign of the Gorenstein parameter decides which component embeds fully faithfully into the other; the zero value removes the exceptional complement and gives equivalence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires a connected graded Noetherian Gorenstein algebra, its duality, admissibility results, and carefully indexed truncation subcategories. The exceptional complement and embedding direction depend on the sign convention for the Gorenstein parameter.
accepted_units.title: Compare two structures through a common ambient decomposition and a signed defect
accepted_units.why_material: It offers a strong general strategy: embed two candidates into one ambient structure, compare their orthogonal complements, and interpret a parameter as the size and direction of the mismatch, with equivalence only at the balanced value.

accepted_units.context_note: For a projective Gorenstein scheme with a suitable very ample line bundle and cohomology vanishing, Serre's quotient description identifies coherent sheaves with the graded quotient category, while duality identifies the geometric canonical-sheaf exponent with the algebraic Gorenstein parameter. The earlier signed comparison then becomes a semiorthogonal embedding in one direction for Fano type, the reverse direction for general type, and an equivalence in the Calabi--Yau case.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The bridge requires connected projective Gorenstein geometry, a very ample line bundle, the stated vanishing outside degrees zero and the dimension, Serre's equivalence, and the source's duality argument. The Fano, general-type, and Calabi--Yau labels do not remove these hypotheses.
accepted_units.title: Transport a geometric defect parameter across an algebraic-categorical bridge
accepted_units.why_material: It shows how a parameter defined in one representation can control categorical directionality in another: first prove the representations equivalent, then transport the invariant and reuse the structural trichotomy.

accepted_units.context_note: When a graded algebra is not generated in degree one, the source replaces ordinary projective geometry by the quotient stack of the punctured affine spectrum under the grading action. Equivariant coherent sheaves correspond to graded modules, and sheaves supported at the removed vertex correspond to torsion, so quotienting produces the same category as coherent sheaves on the stack.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires a commutative connected finitely generated graded algebra and stack/equivariant-sheaf machinery. Passing to ordinary Proj can forget stabilizer or grading information; the quotient-stack representation is essential when degree-one generation fails.
accepted_units.title: Geometricize grading by retaining the group action in a quotient stack
accepted_units.why_material: This is a clean example of repairing a lossy representation: when a coarse geometric quotient forgets grading data, retain the symmetry action and identify algebraic torsion with geometric support at the removed locus.

accepted_units.context_note: A graded matrix factorization is presented as a pair of free modules with alternating maps whose composites are multiplication by a central homogeneous element. Equivalently it is a quasi-periodic curved complex with a two-step shift equal to a grading twist. Morphisms are taken modulo quasi-periodic null homotopies, and mapping cones supply the triangulated structure.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on a finitely generated connected graded algebra and a central homogeneous non-zero-divisor. Exact formulas for degrees, matrices, cone signs, and the shift/twist relation are OCR-sensitive and require source-image verification before exact materialization.
accepted_units.title: Absorb a nonzero square into curvature and periodicity
accepted_units.why_material: It generalizes the usual complex condition by making the obstruction to squaring to zero explicit, then restores homotopical and triangulated reasoning through periodicity, null homotopies, shifts, and cones.

accepted_units.context_note: Taking the cokernel of one factorization map produces a module over the hypersurface quotient because the potential acts by zero. Null-homotopic maps factor through a locally free object and therefore vanish in the singularity quotient. Acyclicity after tensoring with the quotient algebra makes the construction commute with translation and exact triangles.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Uses the exact graded matrix-factorization setup, the quotient algebra by the potential, and the convention that perfect or locally free objects vanish in the singularity category. The commutative diagram and degree shifts are fragmented by extraction.
accepted_units.title: Turn a curved periodic object into its singular quotient invariant
accepted_units.why_material: The construction is a reusable bridge pattern: apply an ordinary invariant, prove that the chosen homotopies land in the class already killed by the target quotient, and separately verify compatibility with shift and triangles.

accepted_units.context_note: Fullness of the cokernel construction is combined with the description of quotient morphisms modulo projective factorizations to prove full faithfulness. Faithfulness is reduced to showing that a cone sent to zero is already null-homotopic. Under finite homological dimension, projective resolutions construct a matrix factorization representing every target object, upgrading the functor to an equivalence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The argument depends on the preceding acyclicity, Ext-vanishing, and zero-detection lemmas; essential surjectivity additionally requires finite homological dimension of the ambient algebra and freeness of graded projectives. The normalized proof has fragmented diagrams and indices.
accepted_units.title: Upgrade a bridge by separating fullness, zero detection, and essential surjectivity
accepted_units.why_material: It exposes a broadly useful equivalence-proof architecture: make morphisms concrete, detect the kernel through cones or homotopies, and construct preimages only after isolating the finiteness condition that makes resolutions terminate appropriately.

accepted_units.context_note: The source composes three established bridges: graded matrix factorizations to the singularity category, the singularity category to the graded quotient category, and that quotient to coherent sheaves on a projective hypersurface or quotient stack. For homogeneous hypersurfaces, the sign of degree minus ambient dimension determines which category contains the other with an exceptional complement, while equality gives equivalence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires positive connected grading, semi-invariance of the potential, finite homological dimension of the polynomial ambient algebra, the hypersurface or quotient-stack presentation, and all hypotheses of the component equivalences. The B-brane terminology is application-specific; the categorical conclusions are conditional mathematical statements.
accepted_units.title: Compose local equivalences while propagating the defect parameter
accepted_units.why_material: It demonstrates disciplined synthesis: chain compatible representation changes, preserve every hypothesis and variance direction, and let a single transported defect parameter explain embedding, complement, or equivalence in the final comparison.

The lens identifier is assignment-routed; overlap with the frozen parent corpus and external novelty were not assessed.

Admissible orthogonals and semiorthogonal decompositions make the retained component and exceptional complement explicit, while a signed parameter controls their order and disappearance. The decompositions are conditional and ordered, not asserted to be canonical; novelty and corpus overlap remain unconfirmed.

The source makes obstructions visible either as maps factoring through projectives or as curvature whose square is multiplication by a potential, then quotients by the corresponding null homotopies. This is source-grounded support for the routed lens, not a claim of independent novelty.
